title: Design one-way parent-to-child VM information sharing
objective: Define a common, least-authority contract for information a parent VM intentionally shares with nested child VMs. Compare read-only MCP resources with push-only snapshots, ensure child access cannot become parent control, and keep network isolation as the primary boundary.

acceptance_criteria.text: Document the parent/child data-flow threat model and distinguish parent-selected information flowing down from child requests/control flowing up; explicitly decide whether request/response MCP satisfies the required one-way semantics or a push-only artifact is required.
Define a versioned, size-bounded schema for parent-selected records with provenance and sensitivity metadata; children cannot enumerate or access unshared records.

Specify a per-child transport and authorization path bound to loopback and an explicit guestfwd/SSH channel; it exposes no arbitrary parent filesystem, command, Docker, network, credential, or write capability.
Specify recursive behavior: each descendant receives only data explicitly selected by its immediate parent, with scoped credentials, revocation, and no inherited parent/ancestor channel.

Record the decision and security limits in VM architecture docs and define adversarial tests for read scope, write attempts, path/URI abuse, child depth/reset, and transport isolation before implementation is accepted.

needed: Inventory current host/guest crossings and browser-auth MCP capability; identify whether any existing channel can expose parent state beyond its intended purpose.
Compare read-only MCP resources with a push-only schema-validated snapshot for strict one-way data flow; document the request-metadata direction tradeoff.
Define adversarial integration tests proving a child cannot read unshared parent data, mutate parent state, invoke arbitrary host actions, or access ancestor channels.
